questions.q: Why does the summary say unpredictability is so seductive?
a: People are pattern-seekers who lose interest once they have figured someone out
Surprises make other people feel uncertain and dependent
Unpredictable people are seen as more powerful
It hides a lack of genuine personality
questions.why: Lesson 1 explains that humans analyse patterns, so breaking them keeps someone interesting.

questions.q: Which seducer type reminds people of their honest, spontaneous childhood self?
a: The Natural, who recalls our honest childhood selves
The Dandy, who defies every social role
The Charmer, who makes us feel comfortable
The Star, who lets us escape our own lives
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes the Natural as a reminder of the playful, spontaneous person we once were.

Shows total devotion and asks for nothing back
Refuses to play any social role at all
Lifts people up by praising their best traits
questions.why: Lesson 2 calls the Coquette a master of the bait-and-switch, which only makes them more desirable.

questions.q: What does the summary say about playing hard to get?
a: Do it not because it works but because you are worth it
Use it only with people you genuinely like
Avoid it, since it makes you seem dishonest
It works best when combined with constant attention
questions.why: Lesson 1 ends by saying you should be hard to get because you are worth it, not as a tactic.

questions.q: What does the summary say about anti-seductive traits?
a: They are easy to spot in others but hard to see in ourselves
They only appear in people who are already insecure
They disappear once you learn the nine types
They are impossible to change after childhood
questions.why: Lesson 3 says spotting these behaviors in others is simple, while recognizing them in yourself is harder.
